value.first: I'd use the Ferber method (graduated check-ins). It's one of the best-studied sleep methods there is, and kids followed for five years showed no harm. The 3am waking is a falling-asleep skill: if he needs you to drift off at bedtime, he needs you again at 3. So start at bedtime: same 20-30 min wind-down, any milk before the book, then into the crib drowsy but awake, say your goodnight phrase, and leave.
value.second: Night 1: wait 3, then 5, then 10 minutes, and 10 for every check after that. Night 2: 5/10/12. Night 3: 10/12/15. Checks are 1-2 min: lights off, same short phrase, then leave even mid-cry. No pickup, no feed. At 3am, restart that night's sequence from its first wait. Expect night 2 or 3 to be worse than night 1. That's the old pattern breaking. If you can't do the waiting, the chair method is the gentler version.
value.third: Nights 4-7, keep stretching: 12/15/17, then 15/17/20, 17/20/25, 20/25/30. It's working when he settles faster and the 3am protest gets shorter. Many families see clear change within the week. If he snores, gasps, or pauses breathing in his sleep, that's worth a doctor visit, since no sleep method fixes it. I'll check in Thursday.
